title: Acute Abdominal Pain Evaluation
description: Evaluation of acute abdominal symptoms with targeted screening for surgical emergencies and peritonitis.

risk_rules.name: Acute Peritoneal / Rigid Abdomen Emergency
risk_rules.reason: Severe abdominal pain accompanied by board-like abdominal rigidity, continuous vomiting, hematemesis, or hemodynamic instability (dizziness, fainting).
risk_rules.possible_concern: Acute surgical abdomen / Viscus perforation / Severe peritonitis

risk_rules.name: Right Lower Quadrant Appendicitis Pattern
risk_rules.reason: Pain migrating from periumbilical region to the right lower quadrant, accompanied by fever, anorexia, or worsening with movement.

risk_rules.name: Right Upper Quadrant / Biliary Colic Pattern
risk_rules.reason: Right upper quadrant pain radiating to the right shoulder/scapula, frequently triggered post-prandially by fatty food, accompanied by fever or nausea.

risk_rules.name: Crampy Generalized Abdominal Pain with Diarrhea
risk_rules.reason: Diffuse diffuse crampy pain associated with nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea without focal localization or peritoneal signs.

risk_rules.name: Mild Epigastric Dyspepsia without Alarming Features
risk_rules.reason: Mild burning or discomfort in upper abdomen related to meals, without weight loss, black stools, vomiting, or progressive severe pain.

possible_conditions.name: Acute appendicitis
possible_conditions.reason_template: Right lower quadrant abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, fever, or movement aggravation.
possible_conditions.caveat: Decision support only. Requires physical examination, lab work (CBC/CRP), and urgent ultrasound or CT scan.

possible_conditions.name: Acute cholecystitis
possible_conditions.reason_template: Right upper quadrant pain with radiation to right back/shoulder and fever or nausea.
possible_conditions.caveat: Requires clinical examination and urgent biliary ultrasound.

possible_conditions.name: Acute gastroenteritis
possible_conditions.reason_template: Cramping abdominal discomfort with watery diarrhea, nausea, and low-grade systemic symptoms.
possible_conditions.caveat: Monitor hydration status; medical review required if unable to keep fluids down.

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Pinpoints anatomical quadrant to isolate appendiceal, biliary, or vascular danger zones.
recommended_questions.question: Where exactly is the pain located in your belly (for example: lower right side, upper right side, or all over)?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Evaluates potential peritonitis and surgical abdomen.
recommended_questions.question: On a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is the pain, and does your belly feel rigid, hard, or hurts when touched?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Checks for inflammatory and obstructive pathology.
recommended_questions.question: Do you have a fever, repeated vomiting, or are you unable to hold down fluids?
Have you noticed any vomiting of blood, coffee-ground material, or dark black tarry stools?
